correctness.rationale: Reconstructed literal zero-inclusive EFX criterion: a two-incoming-edge sink 01 at internal vertex v_j requires outer incoming edges b_(j-2)=0,b_(j+1)=1 and comparisons w_(j-2)>=w_(j-1), w_(j+1)>=w_j. A word with no 01 is 1^a0^(m-a), giving universal lower m+1 and exact minimum for strictly increasing weights. For equal weights the allowed 0011-flanked 01 language has generating function 1/((1-z)^2-z^4), yielding U_m=sum_k binom(m-2k+1,2k+1) and asymptotic coefficient (1/2+1/sqrt5)*phi^m with bounded correction. Arbitrarily small strictly monotone perturbation collapses U_m to m+1. Independently compared literal pair/removal EFX with local condition on 55,986 weighted orientations; finite tests supplement the all-m run argument.

evidence: EFX0 orientation is an allocation of each graph-edge good to an endpoint, with removal of ANY good even if valuer assigns it zero. Existing cycle theorem also reduces EFX0 to forbidden short runs but has cyclic boundary conditions, not path endpoints.

value.rationale: Counting all fair solutions and their sharp sensitivity on the simplest path graph gives an exact, natural measure of fairness prevalence, beyond known existence results. An arbitrarily small coherent change in symmetric positive edge values induces a sharp exponential-to-linear collapse, a motivated structural instability rather than an arbitrary sequence count.
